questions.q: What schema change does Meridian's fulfillment team request, and why?
options: Two new nullable columns and a supporting index on dbo.Orders, to support a delayed-shipment report
A brand-new database to replace MeridianCommerce entirely
Dropping the Orders table and rebuilding it from scratch
Renaming MeridianCommerce to MeridianOrders
questions.explain: EstimatedShipDate and ShipDelayReasonCode, plus a filtered index on EstimatedShipDate, support a new report on orders running behind schedule.

questions.q: Under the new process, how does this schema change get proposed instead of arriving by email?
options: A developer edits the database project on a branch and opens a pull request against meridian-dbaops
The developer runs the ALTER TABLE statement directly against MERSQLPRD01
The change is announced verbally in a stand-up meeting with no written record
It is submitted as a support ticket to Microsoft
questions.explain: The change goes into MeridianCommerce.sqlproj on a branch and through a pull request, giving Priya a real code-review step before anything touches a server.

questions.q: What does SqlPackage.exe do in this pipeline?
options: Publishes the built .dacpac against a target database, comparing schemas and applying the needed changes
Compiles PowerShell scripts into an executable
Sends Teams notifications when a pipeline stage completes
Replaces Git as the pipeline's source control system
questions.explain: SqlPackage.exe is Microsoft's real tool for deploying .dacpac packages, comparing the package against a live database and generating/applying the ALTER or CREATE statements needed.

questions.q: Why does the pipeline deploy to MERSQLDEV01 automatically but require a human approval before deploying to MERSQLPRD01?
options: So a person reviews exactly what will change on production before it happens, while low-risk testing proceeds without a bottleneck
MERSQLDEV01 doesn't actually support automated deployments
Azure DevOps pipelines cannot deploy to production servers under any configuration
There is no real reason — the asymmetry is arbitrary
questions.explain: The environment approval gate is a deliberate choke point: automatic where the risk is low, human-reviewed where it isn't.

questions.q: What does the prepared rollback script for this change do?
options: Drops the new index and the two new nullable columns from dbo.Orders
Restores the entire MeridianCommerce database from the last full backup
Reverts the pipeline YAML file to its previous version
Nothing — nullable column additions never need a rollback plan
questions.explain: Because the change is a simple nullable addition with no data migration, the rollback is a small, checked-in script that drops the index and the two new columns.
